title: Residue field extensions of an etale morphism are separable algebraic
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be an etale morphism of schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism], let $x\in X$, and let $r:\kappa(f(x))\to\kappa(x)$ be the field homomorphism induced by $f$ on residue fields [def-weil-residue-field]. Then $\kappa(x)$, viewed as a field extension of $\kappa(f(x))$ through $r$, is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]: every element of $\kappa(x)$ is algebraic and separable over $\kappa(f(x))$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 02G8 (morphisms-lemma-unramified-etale-fibres, line 7827), part (1): for an unramified morphism the extension kappa(x)/kappa(f(x)) is finite separable; an etale morphism is unramified (Morphisms, Lemma 02GK = morphisms-lemma-etale-smooth-unramified; directly from def-weil-etale-morphism, which defines etale as flat, locally of finite presentation and unramified)
